applicability: Any chain of successive percentage discounts applied one after another to the running price. For discounts of a% then b%, with 0 <= a <= 100 and 0 <= b <= 100, the fraction of the price still to pay is the product of the keep-fractions: (1 - a/100)(1 - b/100), so the total discount is a + b - ab/100 percent. This is exact - not an approximation - for every a and b in that range, for any starting price, for any number of stacked discounts (keep multiplying keep-fractions), and in either order, because multiplication commutes. It covers only percentage discounts taken off the running price; a fixed-amount coupon ('10 off') is not a percentage and is outside the rule, and so is a coupon whose terms say it is calculated on the ORIGINAL price rather than on the reduced one.
carry_case: Adding the two percentages. The tempting simple rule 'a% off then b% off = (a+b)% off' is wrong whenever both discounts are nonzero, because it misses the -ab/100 term. Concrete break, the drawn example itself: 10% off then 80% off is 82% off, not 90% off - a 100 item goes 100 -> 90 -> 18, and 18 paid means 82 off, while the add rule predicts 10 left. Most memorable break: 50% off then 50% off is not free, it leaves 25% of the price. Adding agrees with the correct rule only when a = 0 or b = 0.

steps.instruction: Multiply what's left, don't add what's off

worked_example.result: 18% of the price left, i.e. 82% off (100 → 90 → 18)

operand_draw.declared_mapping: discount_percent = 10 × draw, so draws [1, 8] give the discounts 10% and 80%. The range 1..9 is the set of whole-ten discounts 10%..90%, declared before the draw. The mapping is presentational only - it keeps the on-card arithmetic to one decimal place - and the method is exact for every value in the range, so no draw could have been rejected on mathematical grounds.
operand_draw.cli_note: core/pipeline/lib/sampling.mjs CLI self-guard (import.meta.url vs process.argv[1]) does not fire on Windows paths, so the draw was taken by importing draw() from that same module with the seed and spec above; verifyDraw replays it.
